name: Nūr al-Dīn Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Ushmūnī
summary: Egyptian grammarian whose Manhaj al-sālik, 'Sharḥ al-Ushmūnī', became the commentary on the Alfiyya most read at al-Azhar, and the base of al-Ṣabbān's gloss.
bio: Al-Ushmūnī, whose family came from Ushmūn in Upper Egypt, taught grammar, law and logic in Cairo at the end of the Mamluk age. His Manhaj al-sālik ilā Alfiyyat Ibn Mālik explains the poem verse by verse, gathering what Ibn al-Nāẓim, al-Murādī and Ibn Hishām had said before him into one clear and full text; it became the Azhar's commentary of the Alfiyya, and al-Ṣabbān's gloss on it is the last great work on the poem. He also put other books into verse.

works.title: Manhaj al-sālik ilā Alfiyyat Ibn Mālik
works.arabic: مَنْهَجُ السَّالِكِ إِلَى أَلْفِيَّةِ ابْنِ مَالِك

uncertain: His year of death is uncertain: the TDV gives 918/1513, other sources about 900/1495 or 929/1523.
